01 • CURRENT OBSERVATION

From activity feed to admissions storytelling

The school already has genuine activities, achievements and student moments. The opportunity is to organise that content around what prospective parents need to see before choosing a school.

Keep event coverage
Add parent-focused stories
Give every post a purpose

“I wouldn't remove the existing activity content because it proves the school is active. I would add a second layer: content that helps a prospective parent understand why their child should study here.”

Content
Enquiry

22 • FIRST 30 DAYS

Start small, test, then scale

Build the system first, pilot a few repeatable formats, measure response and expand what works rather than launching everything at once.

Week 1: audit + brand kit
Week 2: POV + achiever pilots
Week 3: Studio + parent Q&A
Week 4: measure + optimise

“I wouldn't try to launch every idea in week one. I would build the foundation, test a few formats, look at the data and feedback, then scale the ideas that are actually working.”

INSTAGRAM AUDIT • CURRENT PROFILE

Strong activity. Clearer positioning can make it work harder.

What is already workingThe page immediately shows real students, school activities, achievements and a busy school community.
Opportunity: bio positioningMake the bio more parent-focused: location, key school information, admissions status and one clear action such as “Book a campus visit”.
Opportunity: HighlightsOrganise Highlights around parent decisions: Admissions, Campus, Academics, Activities, Achievements, Transport and FAQs.
Why it mattersA new parent should understand the school and know the next step within seconds of opening the profile.

“The account already proves that the school is active. My first improvement would be to make the profile easier for a prospective parent to understand and act on. I want the bio and Highlights to work almost like a mini admissions landing page.”

INSTAGRAM AUDIT • VISUAL IDENTITY

The feed has energy, but not one consistent visual language.

KeepReal photographs, cultural colour, student work and authentic school moments.
ImproveStandardise designed posts, typography, Reel covers and recurring-series templates using the proposed brand palette.
GoalPhotography can stay colourful; branded graphics should still be recognisable as Shining Star before the username is read.

“I am not suggesting making every photograph the same colour. School life should look colourful. I would create consistency in the designed elements—covers, fonts, title placement and templates—so the overall feed feels like one brand.”

INSTAGRAM AUDIT • FROM DOCUMENTATION TO STORY

Don't only show what happened. Explain why a parent should care.

Current patternMany posts successfully document events and celebrations after they happen.
Next layerBuild the post around a parent or student benefit: confidence, creativity, wellbeing, teamwork, communication or learning.
Stronger structureHook → human story → proof → simple call to action.
ExampleInstead of only “Father's Day Celebration”, tell one short parent-child story or capture a parent reaction and connect it to school community.

“The events are useful proof, so I would keep them. The change is in the storytelling. I want every important post to answer: what does this tell a prospective parent about the experience their child could have here?”

INSTAGRAM AUDIT • ACHIEVEMENT CONTENT

Turn a winning moment into a story people remember.

Current strengthThe school already celebrates student awards, competitions and performances.
ImprovementFor major achievements, add a 30–60 second student interview rather than relying only on a group photo or poster.
QuestionsWhat did you achieve? How did you prepare? What was difficult? Who helped you? What is next?
ResultThe achievement becomes a student story, gives parents something meaningful to share, and shows the school's support behind the result.

“This is already strong material. I would simply extract more value from it. If a student wins something significant, I want to hear from that student and show the journey—not only the final certificate or stage photograph.”

INSTAGRAM AUDIT • CAPTIONS & CONVERSION

Make captions easier to scan—and give interested parents a next step.

ObservationDetailed captions provide context, but long blocks can hide the strongest message on a mobile screen.
ImprovementLead with a strong first line, use shorter paragraphs, keep the human outcome near the top, then add supporting detail.
Add a relevant CTAWhere the post supports recruitment, finish with a natural next step: explore the school, ask a question, register for an event or book a visit.
ImportantNot every post needs to sell. Community posts can simply build trust; conversion CTAs should be used where they make sense.

“I would not put ‘apply now’ under every post. But when content is useful for a prospective family, I would make the next step obvious. The first line earns attention, the story builds interest, and the CTA gives that interest somewhere to go.”

23 • STRATEGIC FRAMEWORK

Every campaign needs a job

Use three objectives to keep the marketing plan focused instead of treating every idea as a separate campaign.

BUILD THE BRAND
BUILD THE COMMUNITY
DRIVE ADMISSIONS

“Before approving a campaign, I would ask what job it is doing. It should strengthen the brand, strengthen the community, contribute to admissions—or ideally connect more than one.”

FINAL THOUGHT

Don't just show
the school.
Let families experience it.

Every campaign should do at least one of three things: strengthen the brand, strengthen the community, or contribute to admissions.

BUILD THE COMMUNITY

DRIVE ADMISSIONS
